title: LibPreemptible: Enabling Fast, Adaptive, and Hardware-Assisted User-Space Scheduling
problem: Modern cloud applications suffer from high tail latencies due to highly-dispersive request distributions, and existing scheduling solutions either require significant OS modifications, have scalability limitations, or fail to utilize full hardware capabilities.
motivation: Reducing tail latencies is critical for cloud application performance and user experience.
method: LibPreemptible implements a preemptive user-level threading library using three key techniques: a fast, lightweight hardware mechanism for delivering timed interrupts; a general-purpose user-level scheduling interface; and an API for users to specify adaptive scheduling policies. The system avoids kernel modifications by operating entirely at the user level while leveraging hardware support for timer delivery.
key_novelty: Hardware-assisted delivery of timed interrupts to enable efficient preemptive user-level scheduling without kernel modifications.
contributions: Fast and lightweight hardware mechanism for timed interrupt delivery to user-space
API for expressing application-specific adaptive scheduling policies
Significant tail latency and throughput improvements over Shinjuku without kernel changes

metrics.speedup: Significant tail latency and throughput improvements vs Shinjuku
metrics.other: Tail latency reduction and throughput gains across varying workloads
